column1: Housing census – Conventional dwellings – Time series from 2011 on
column2: The Housing census included in the Register-based census and in the Register-based labour market statistics is a complete survey of the buildings and dwellings and their attributes for the reference date 31 October. The Register-based census and the Register-based labour market statistics are conducted by using information from administrative registers. The main data source for the Housing census is the Buildings- and dwellings register of Statistics Austria. The characteristics and definitions are based on the EU regulation on population and housing censuses and the Austrian Register-based census act (BGBl. I. Nr. 33/2006). For a detailed description of the methods used and for further information see: https://www.statistik.at/en/statistics/population-and-society/housing/stock-of-buildings https://www.statistik.at/en/statistics/population-and-society/housing/stock-of-dwellings https://www.statistik.at/fileadmin/shared/QM/Standarddokumentationen/B_1/std_b_abgestimmte_erwerbsstatistik.pdf (German only) This database contains the results for all conventional dwellings. The dwelling stock in Vienna does not include apartments without residents, that were built between 2012 and 2023 as a result of extension, construction or conversion work. Conventional dwellings are structurally separate premises which are designed for permanent human habitation at a fixed location, with direct access from the street or from a public staircase. They consist of one room or suite of rooms as well as side rooms. The existence of a kitchen or kitchenette is not crucial. Rooms in hotels, student residencies and similar buildings are not counted as conventional dwellings. .) Territorial structure of 2024. .) Updating: annually last update: [2026-06-09] .) Contact details: Directorate social statistics For general enquiries: +43 1 711 28-7070 In case of special enquiries please contact registerzaehlung@statistik.gv.at .) Please note: For data privacy protection reasons, the statistical disclosure control method of "record swapping" has been used on a part of the data. For analyses based on very small cell values, no reliable assertions can be made.

Refers to the location of the building in which the dwelling is located, at the reference date 31 October of the respective year according to the Austrian administrative territorial structure valid in 2024. Other Metadata: https://www.statistik.at/en/services/tools/services/regional-information/regional-divisions

column1: Occupancy status of the dwelling [partly ABO]
column2: Classifies if there are persons, who are counted as part of the population at the reference date 31 October, usually resident in the dwelling.

There is at least one person, who is counted as part of the population at the reference date 31 October, usually resident in the dwelling. In addition, the dwelling might also be used as a seasonal or secondary residence.

There are no persons, who are counted as part of the population at the reference date 31 October, usually resident in the dwelling, but at least one person uses the dwelling as a seasonal or secondary residence.
There are no persons, who are counted as part of the population at the reference date 31 October, usually resident in the dwelling, and there are no seasonal or secondary residences.

column1: Useful floor space in square meters per occupant
column2: Describes the "density standard" of the dwellings referring to the average useful floor space per occupant.

column2: Includes churches and other buildings for religious purposes.

Type of ownership of the building in which the dwelling is located. If the ownership of a building is divided between groups (co-ownership), the owner is defined as the one holding the highest share.
